title: 「Needless to say」表示「不用多說／不言而喻」
titleZh: 「Needless to say」表示「不用多說／不言而喻」

source.file: Sentence Structure 214 -「Needless to say」表示「不用多說／不言而喻」.pdf

example: Needless to say, public money should be used responsibly.
exampleZh: 不用多說，公帑應該以負責任的方式運用。

examples.en: Needless to say, public money should be used responsibly.
examples.zh: 不用多說，公帑應該以負責任的方式運用。
examples.highlight: Needless to say, public money should be used responsibly.

meaning.zh: 本課練習目標句型：Needless to say, + complete clause。

rules.zh: 後面須接完整句子 Needless to say 後面須有主語和動詞。 （不用多說，安全最重要。）
rules.en: Follow Needless to say with a complete clause containing a subject and verb. Correct: Needless to say, safety comes first. Incorrect: Needless to say, the importance of safety.
examples: Correct: Needless to say, safety comes first.
Incorrect: Needless to say, the importance of safety. ✗

rules.zh: 後面通常使用逗號 在本課所學的標準句型中，Needless to say 放在句首，後面加逗號。 （不用多說，大家都很失望。）
rules.en: Normally put a comma after the opening phrase. In the standard pattern taught here, write: Needless to say, everyone was disappointed.
examples: Needless to say, everyone was disappointed.

rules.zh: 本句型通常不加 that 本練習採用最自然和最常見的句式： 不要寫成：
rules.en: Normally do not add that. This exercise uses the most natural and common form: Needless to say, the plan needs more work. Do not write: Needless to say that the plan needs more work.
examples: Needless to say, the plan needs more work. ✓
Needless to say that the plan needs more work. ✗

rules.zh: 只用於明顯或可以預料的事情 不要使用 Needless to say 引出尚未證實、具有爭議或令讀者意外的說法。 （不用多說，駕駛者必須遵守交通燈號。） （除非所有人都已同意，否則這項說法未必是不言而喻的。）
rules.en: Use the phrase only for something obvious or expected, not for an unproven, controversial or surprising assertion. Natural: Needless to say, drivers must obey traffic lights. Unnatural without prior agreement: Needless to say, this is the only possible solution.
examples: Natural: Needless to say, drivers must obey traffic lights.
Needless to say, this is the only possible solution.

rules.zh: 它可以帶有強調語氣 這個句型不只是說「很明顯」，也表示說話者認為這件事是基本常識、合理責任或自然結果。 因此，使用時應避免帶有高高在上或輕視別人意見的語氣。
rules.en: The phrase can add emphasis. It does more than label something obvious: it can present a point as basic common sense, a reasonable duty or a natural consequence. Use it carefully so that you do not sound condescending or dismissive of other views.

benefits.zh: 能立即表示事情十分明顯 讀者或聽者一看到 Needless to say，便知道接下來的內容是合乎常理、可以預料或大家理應知 道的。 （不用多說，兒童需要一個安全的學習環境。）
benefits.en: It immediately marks a point as obvious. On hearing or reading Needless to say, the audience expects a reasonable, predictable or commonly understood statement: Needless to say, children need a safe place to learn.

benefits.zh: 能把較長的說法縮短 你不必每次都使用較長的 It is obvious that...。 （顯然，公帑應該以負責任的方式運用。） （不用多說，公帑應該以負責任的方式運用。） 第二句更直接，也更有力。
benefits.en: It shortens a longer expression such as It is obvious that .... Compare: It is obvious that public money should be used responsibly. Needless to say, public money should be used responsibly. The second version is more direct and forceful.

benefits.zh: 能引出自然或可以預料的結果 當前文已經提供足夠背景時，可以使用這個句型引出讀者早已預料到的結果。 （球隊已有數月沒有練習。不用多說，他們輸掉了比賽。）
benefits.en: It introduces a natural or predictable outcome after the context has supplied enough background: The team had not practised for months. Needless to say, they lost the match.

benefits.zh: 能避免重複使用 obviously 或 of course 這個句型為你提供另一種表達「顯然」的方法，令說話和寫作不會不斷重複相同的開場方式。
benefits.en: It avoids repeatedly using obviously or of course. The frame provides another way to express obviousness and varies the openings used in speech and writing.

benefits.zh: 能令論點顯得更有把握 在討論基本責任、常識或合理後果時，這個句型可以令語氣更堅定。 不過，它帶有一定的強調意味，因此不宜在短文中過度使用。
benefits.en: It makes a point sound more confident when discussing basic duties, common sense or reasonable consequences. Because it carries emphasis, however, do not overuse it in a short text.

questions.answer: Needless to say, in a hospital, patient safety must come before convenience or cost.
questions.answerZh: 不用多說，在醫院，病人安全必須比便利或成本優先。
questions.highlight: Needless to say, in a hospital, patient safety must come before convenience or cost.

questions.prompt: If the same mistake keeps happening, common sense tells us that the process needs to be reviewed.

questions.prompt: It should be beyond dispute that people affected by a policy should be told clearly how it will affect their lives.
questions.promptZh: 受政策影響的人應該獲得清晰說明，知道政策會如何影響其生活；這一點不應存在爭議。
questions.answer: Needless to say, people affected by a policy should be told clearly how it will affect their lives.
